title: Feasibility of a Biobehavioral Intervention for Older Adults With Persistent Low Back Pain
official: ReLOAD: Development and Feasibility Testing of a Biobehavioral Intervention for Older Adults With Persistent Low Back Pain
summary: This study will develop and evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a targeted biobehavioral intervention for adults aged 60 years and older with persistent low back pain who are receiving outpatient physical therapy. The intervention addresses stress-related cognitive appraisal and coping behaviors that may contribute to disability. Twenty participants will complete six individual sessions with a licensed physical therapist. Sessions include education, mindfulness-based breathing exercises, cognitive reframing, guided motor imagery, graded exposure to movement, activity pacing, and individualized maintenance strategies. Participants will complete questionnaires before and after the intervention to assess pain, physical function, psychological distress, and feasibility outcomes.

interventions.name: Biobehavioral Intervention for Persistent Low Back Pain

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Age 60 years or older.
* Persistent low back pain for at least 3 months.
* Currently receiving care through Duke Douglas Street Physical Therapy.

Exclusion Criteria

* Inability to provide informed consent.
* Significant cognitive impairment that prevents meaningful participation (as determined by study physical therapist).
* Medical conditions that preclude participation in physical therapy activities (as determined by study physical therapist).
* Progressive neurologic disorders significantly affecting mobility (as determined by study physical therapist).
* Current participation in another intervention study targeting low back pain.
